newsitem.title: BRAZIL: South American port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: South American port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

BRAZIL March 4 - Vitoria - Vessels berthed, 1 granite loader, 1 bulk malt discharger, 1 general cargo loader, 1 container/general cargo discharger/loader, 1 container discharger, 1 pig iron loader. Tubarao - 3 Iron ore loaders, 1 petroleum discharger. Praia Mole - 3 Steel products loaders, 2 coal dischargers. Portocel - 1 Cellulose loader. 24 Vessels waiting in roads.

Santos - Vessels berthed, 1 bulk lpg discharger, 1 gasoline loader, 3 full container dischargers, 3 full container loaders/dischargers, 1 full container loader, 1 bulk fertiliser discharger, 1 bulk cement discharger, 2 bulk chemical products dischargers, 1 sulphur discharger, 1 bulk wheat discharger, 1 general cargo/container loader,discharger, 1 frozen juice loader, 2 salt dischargers, 2 general cargo dischargers. 9 Vessels waiting in roads, 64 due.

Private terminals - Cosipa - 1 Iron ore discharger, 2 steel products loaders, 1 coal discharger. Paranagua - Stevedores are on a go-slow action from 3/3 to 4/3, and have announced a strike from 5/3 until 7/3. Pending devopments of negotiations in Paranagua, there is a possibility of adherence by the stevedores in 14 other ports, but stevedores will work normally during the weekend of 8/3 and 9/3. Vessels berthed, 1 container discharger, 4 general cargo dischargers, 1 fertiliser discharger, 1 general cargo loader, 1 reefer loader, 2 pellets loaders, 2 soya loaders. 21 Vessels waiting in roads of which for loading, 1 reefer, 12 pellets, 1 general cargo, 5 soya, 2 container vessels for discharging. 28 Vessels due during next 7 days.

Sao Paulo - On 23/2 the regular cargo and passenger services of the state of Sao Paulo railway company were paralysed by its personnel. The dispute was judged on 3/3 by the superior labour court which granted a 10 percent readjustment to the personnel who immediately resumed operations. Itajai - Stevedores on strike. Rio Grande - Vessels berthed, 2 full container loaders, 2 wheat dischargers, 1 fuel discharger, 1 chemical products discharger, 1 fertiliser discharger, vessels due.

Rio de Janeiro - Vessels berthed, 1 general cargo/steel products discharger, 1 wheat discharger, 2 steel products, 1 general cargo/container discharger, 1 caustic soda discharger, 1 general cargo/container loader. Tecon - 2 Vessels, 28 due. Sao Sebastiao - Vessels berthed - Tebar - 2 Vessels. Commercial quay - 1 Vessel. One Vessel waiting in roads, 8 due.

CHILE, March 3 - Arica - Two vessels working normally, 3 berths vacant, 10 vessels due during the week. Antofagasta - Three vessels berthed, 3 berths available. 7 Vessels due during the week for loading and discharging concentrates, bulk copper, containers, general cargo. Valparaiso - Six vessels berthed working normally, 3 berths vacant, 1 berth out of service. 28 Vessels due, 1 day delay can be expected. San Antonio - Four vessels operating, 4 berths vacant, 15 vessels due, no waiting time.

Conception Bay ports - Talcahuano - One vessel operating normally, 1 due, none in roads. San Vicente - Two vessels operating, 1 berth available, 3 vessels due during the week. 1 Day berthing delay expected. Navy pier (Molo 500) - 3 Vessel due. Steel pier - 1 Vessel due. Coronel pier - 2 Vessels in terminal, 1 due. Oil terminal - 1 Vessel in terminal, 1 due. Lirquen - Four vessels berthed, 2 berths vacant, 5 vessels due during the week. Penco - No vessels in port. Puerto Montt - One coaster berthed, 3 vessels due during the week. Punta Arenas - One vessel berthed, 6 vessels due.

PERU, March 3 - Callao - Eight vessels in bay, 10 in pier (general cargo,containers), no berthing delays. Paita - Two vessels in bay, 3 in pier (fishmeal,coffee), no berthing delays. Bayovar, Pisco - No vessels. Talara - One vessel in bay, 1 in pier (oil), no berthing delays. Chimbote - One vessel in bay, 2 in pier (fishmeal), no berthing delays. Ilo - One general cargo vessel in bay, no berthing delays.

VENEZUELA, March 3 - Puerto Cabello - Two vessels anchored. 7 Vessels berthed of which 1 grain, 2 general cargo, 2 bulk cargo, 2 containers. Piers 1 and 2 closed. Guanta - One vessel anchored, 3 general cargo vessels berthed. March 4 - Orinoco river - Draft 31 ft. 6 in. Puerto Ordaz - One vessel loading iron ore, 6 vessels due. Palua - One passenger vessel, 1 vessel due. Boca Grande - One vessel loading iron ore, 2 vessels due. Matanzas - Six vessels loading steel products, 3 vessels due. Venalum - One vessel loading aluminium. San Felix - One vessel discharging anodes, 1 vessel due. Punta Cuchillo - One vessel loading refined products, 1 vessel due. Puerto Cabello - 13 Vessels loading/discharging generals, 17 due.

Guanta - One vessel loading/discharging generals, 5 vessels due. Maracaibo - One vessel discharging generals. Puerto Miranda - Three vessels loading crude oil. Buoy B71 - Two vessels loading coal. Palmarejo Sur - One vessel loading crude oil. El Tablazo - Three vessels loading urea. Punta Camacho - One vessel loading crude. Bajo Grande - Refined products terminal - 1 Vessel loading crude. San Francisco - Two vessels loading crude. No vessels at La Salina, Puerto Palma, San Lorenzo, La Ceiba. Amuay - Two vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 4 vessels loading refined products. Cardon - Three vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 4 vessels loading products. All ports working normally.
